contributions.statement: Give a Java test-generation agent static-analysis dependency context (classes, constructors, call graph) through tool calls rather than having it infer project structure.
contributions.evidence: Table IV: removing the knowledge graph drops line coverage 92.3 to 75.7 and mutation 83.7 to 66.1; audit notes the paper never says what context the ablated variant gets, so this may just be 'remove all repo context'.

contributions.statement: Expect agent-generated Java unit tests to score far lower on mutation on private code than on Defects4J (55% vs 84% here) and re-measure on the team's own repositories before trusting published numbers.
contributions.evidence: Table VI: UTXXX industrial set 55.38% mutation vs 83.69% public, but the model also changed (Qwen3-30B vs GPT-4o), so leakage and model effects are confounded.

reason: The context-retrieval lesson is shown with closed data and a cleaner industrial design in CATGen; the public-vs-private gap is confounded by a model switch. Nothing qualifies as new and strong.
